correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and 1<=k<=floor(n/2), the edge derivative is an onto isometry to the zero-sum l-infinity hyperplane. Averaging any real projection under rotation gives the unique spectral Fourier multiplier, proving unrestricted optimality. Its exact operator norm is the l1 quotient distance of sampled cosine coefficients to constants; the minimum is a median. Elementary trigonometric sums prove all three residue formulas and m=2 boundary. The explicit inequalities establish strictly noncontractive norm for every m>=5 and the limit 4/pi. The packaged checker has 1998 cosine-sum checks and 992 independent LP tests; the proof, not these tests, establishes the infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Full primary comparison with Cúth-Doucha group-action projection theorem and full published scientific records on cycle numerical index, three-frequency endpoint Fourier projection, and two-frequency L1 point concentration found no implication of the zero-sum Lipschitz harmonic projection formula. The former concerns orbit-fixed subspaces, the numerical index is a different operator invariant, the three-frequency projection acts on full l-infinity instead of the zero-sum hyperplane, and the two-frequency result is a complex-character point-concentration ratio rather than a real projection norm. Standard averaging and median duality are not claimed as new; the substantive exact all-order evaluation and contractivity classification are. Bibliographic residual risk remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent formula may appear in earlier unindexed approximation theory or finite cyclic Fourier interpolation under different terminology; this was not exhaustively excluded.

One closely related group-isometry paper (arxiv:2402.08266) was only used for contextual discovery; a full comparison to every subsidiary theorem there was not made. Its stated scope is isometries rather than minimal projections.

value.rationale: This determines a natural Banach-space complementability invariant for the whole family of real single-harmonic subspaces on finite metric cycles. The conclusion is not merely a numerical example: it gives all dimensions and frequency orders, the exact minimum over arbitrary projections, the complete contractivity threshold m<=4, and the uniform asymptotic 4/pi. The zero-sum Lipschitz derivative changes the answer substantially from conventional full-space endpoint Fourier projection norms. This is a motivated structural classification rather than an arbitrary slice.
